newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy debates how to handle Albanian refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: Italy debates how to handle Albanian refugee crisis.

text.p: A ship with hundreds of Albanians on board headed for port in Italy on Saturday and Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said the country should brace for a mass influx of refugees.

Italian coastguards said an Albanian navy ship had been intercepted in the Adriatic and was being escorted to the southeast port of Brindisi. Initial estimates said 200 to 300 people, many of them children, were on board.
"We are facing a massive phenomenon because unfortunately this week the Albanian state has fallen apart," Napolitano told reporters at a drugs conference in Naples.
"But we are prepared for every eventuality."
In Brindisi, the main destination of shelter from the chaos in Albania, national police and immigration chiefs were meeting to discuss ways to cope with the developing exodus.

The police headquarters in Brindisi said that by 1000 GMT, a total of 961 Albanians had arrived since the troubles started. They said 83 of them were deserting soldiers or sailors, many of whom have sought political asylum.
Four more boats arrived shortly after midday (1100 GMT), including one fishing boat with around 190 on board and another with about 75 people.

The problem of what to do with the refugees has become a pressing issue for Italy, already a magnet for Albanian illegal immigrants, which does not want to do anything that might encourage tens of thousands to seek refuge.
The exodus has raised fears in Italy of a repeat of the tide of 40,000 Albanians who flooded into southeast ports in 1991 after Stalinist rule crumbled in Europe's poorest state.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) on Friday urged Italy and Greece to allow Albanians fleeing widespread turmoil sparked by the collapse of shady pyramid savings schemes to enter and stay "as long as necessary".
Napolitano said Italy, and particularly the southeast Puglia region, was accommodating the Albanians at various sites that had been earmarked for such an eventuality.
"The situation is very different from last Saturday, when the question of asylum was raised for individuals and groups. Now we are unfortunately facing a massive phenomenon," he said.

The chief of police in the Adriatic port of Ancona said the Interior Ministry had advised all chiefs of police in coastal cities to prepare for the eventual arrival of Albanians from parts of the country such as Puglia that no longer had space.
Officials in the port of Bari said they were accommodating 204 Albanians in various centres in the province.
They added, however, that most of the latest arrivals had been fishermen who said they had fled to protect their ships from being assaulted by desperate mobs at home.

Brindisi police chief Antonio Ruggiero told reporters the situation was "absolutely under control" although the port was full after the latest arrivals. They included a convoy of 20 to 30 vessels, which had earlier stretched out for about 15 miles.
"The police are doing their best to ensure that the presence of the Albanians is not noticed by the local population, and certainly not as a problem," Ruggiero said.
He added that police had been asking the Red Cross and local social services for several days to provide nappies and baby care products as well as food for the Albanians.
An Albanian military helicopter landed in southern Italy with 33 refugees on board, including five children, while scores more docked on rusty merchant ships and fishing boats.
About half of the 90 refugees on board two fishing boats that entered the small harbour at Savelletri, near Brindisi, on Saturday were children, mostly under the age of 10.
A pregnant women who arrived in the southernmost port of Otranto on Friday with her husband and two children, gave birth to a boy on Saturday in a nearby hospital.
